To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proportion of freshmen in a given class who fail in the first year is a function of the mean high-school rank of the freshmen, that the mean high-school ranks of the freshmen are a function of the number of students who apply, the number admitted, and the number of students enrolled, and that the mean high school rank of the students enrolled is a function of their mean freshman-year grade.

the number of students who would fail to meet the requirements for admission if they were raised to the level of the upper 10 per cent of the high-school graduates in 1947 would be approximately twice as large as the total enrollment in 1947.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems: (I) The effect of changing admissions standards on the size and quality of the entering class.
the effects on the university and its students of changing the standards of admission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the number of persons who are admitted should be limited by the size of the university's resources and facilities, that a large proportion of the students admitted should be selected on the basis of their academic promise, and that a smaller number should be selected because they are capable of benefiting from a university education.
selective admissions should be used as one means of achieving a desirable balance between the objectives of higher learning and the needs of society for trained men and women.
, if the objective of a university were to educate the best and the brightest, then the admissions standards should be high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, if we were to raise the academic standards for college admission, the number of students who would be admitted to the university would be smaller, the academic achievement of those students would be better, and the proportion of students who would drop out would be smaller.
we have found a strong relationship between the ability of the students admitted and their subsequent academic success.
we can predict the effect of changes in the admissions standards on enrollments and on the academic success of students, but not on the values which the university is to serve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the present system of admissions is a good one.
the number of students who graduate from college is not a good measure of the quality of a college.
selective admissions are an important part of the academic program of a university.
